newsitem.title: UK: Gold, dollar drop, European bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold, dollar drop, European bourses mixed.

text.p: Gold slid to new 12-year lows on Monday as investors sold amid market fears that central banks could offload more of their official gold reserves.
On currency markets, the dollar lost ground with news of a rising Japanese trade surplus boosting the yen and renewed jitters on European economic and monetary union (EMU) helping to aid the mark.
The Frankfurt bourse hit another record high and Paris made moderate gains but fears of higher interest rates spooked the London stock market.
U.S. blue chip stocks on Wall Street, meanwhile, were up around a quarter of a percentage point after half an hour of trading following Friday's U.S. holiday.
Gold dropped to a low of $314.10 an ounce at one point, down more than $10 from Friday, before recovering to around $317.35.
"It would take a Martian to be bullish at this point," said Andy Smith, precious metals analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland.
"Expect an orgy of selling over the next few weeks," a bullion dealer added.
The bullion price plunged to 12-year lows last week after the Reserve Bank of Australia said it had sold 167 tonnes from its gold reserves.

Following disposals earlier in the 1990s by the Belgian and Dutch central banks, this pushed already nervous investors to sell for fear more central banks would get rid of some of the 35,000 tonnes of gold they own.
Gold has now lost around $50 since January, putting the future of some mines in doubt.
The yen was boosted to four-week highs around 112 to the dollar after news of a 129.3-percent year-on-year gain in Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of June.

The dollar also came under pressure from the mark as the pound lost around two pfennigs after data showed a sharp drop in British industrial output, which analysts attributed mainly to sterling's strength.
The U.S. currency suffered further from market nerves over Europe's nervous progress towards EMU.
As some senior German politicians continue to speak out for a delay in EMU, the mark has gained favour in the short term.

In an interview in the Financial Times, Bavarian prime minister Edmund Stoiber, a member of the Christian Social Union party of Theo Waigel, Germany's finance minister, said an EMU delay would be preferable to a weak single currency.
Currency dealers said that although the market still expected EMU to start on time in 1999, calls for a delay have raised some doubts, prompting mixed views on what that could mean for the dollar.

"You can argue there will be safe-haven buying of marks because the soft euro is questioned, or that investors will want to get out of Euorope altogether and into dollars, sterling or maybe Swiss francs," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in London.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, meanwhile, said the Group of 10 top industrial nations would continue to monitor currency markets closely but avoided comment on recent strength of the dollar.
In equity markets, German shares advanced to more records as uncertainty faded and traders prepared to attack the key 4,000 point level on the 30-share DAX index.
"The risk in the German share market at the moment is not to be invested in it," Susanne Schneemayer at Hypo-Research said in a market commentary.

After early gains, the London stock market was dragged down by a fall in futures amid speculation that the newly-independent Bank of England would raise interest rates this week to keep the economy from overheating.
"We are under a bit of pressure at the thought of higher rates and after last week's gains, a small correction is not unreasonable," said the head of equity trading at one London brokerage.

Britain's latest building society-turned-bank to float on the stock market, Woolwich, provided a rare bright point. It topped its tipped debut level of around 320 pence at 337 but was well below an earlier high of 370.
The Paris bourse erased early losses, prompted by the lower dollar and technical reasons, to show a gain of around a third of a percentage point by mid-afternoon.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was around 112.32 yen and 1.7445 marks, compared with 113.74 and 1.7565 in late European business on Friday. Sterling was around 2.9370 marks versus 2.9597 late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 9.6 points or 0.20 percent at 4,803.2 but well above its low of 4,776.4.

FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 30.31 points or 0.77 percent at a record close of 3,972.84. In later electronic trade the IBIS DAX index was up more than one percent at 3,987.76 after earlier coming within three points of the 4,000 level.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 10.52 points or 0.36 percent higher at 2,945.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold was quoted around $317.35 an ounce in mid-afternoon in Europe, up from its lows but well down from Friday's late $324.50. Silver declined 13 cents to $4.42.
